source_text: Τετάρτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγένοντο οἱ φωστῆρες.Ἐπειδὴ ὁ θεὸς προγνώστης ὢν ἠπίστατο τὰς φλυαρίας τῶν ματαίων φιλοσόφων, ὅτι ἤμελλον λέγειν ἀπὸ τῶν στοιχείων εἶναι τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς φυόμενα, πρὸς τὸ ἀθετεῖν τὸν θεόν· ἵν᾿ οὖν τὸ ἀληθὲς δειχθῇ, προγενέστερα γέγονεν τὰ φυτὰ καὶ τὰ σπέρματα τῶν στοιχείων· τὰ γὰρ μεταγενέστερα οὐ δύναται ποιεῖν τὰ αὐτῶν προγενέστερα. Ταῦτα δὲ δεῖγμα καὶ τύπον ἐπέχει μεγάλου μυστηρίου.Ὁ γὰρ ἥλιος ἐν τύπῳ θεοῦ ἐστιν, ἡ δὲ σελήνη ἀνθρώπου. Καὶ ὥσπερ ὁ ἥλιος πολὺ διαφέρει τῆς σελήνης δυνάμει καὶ δόξῃ, οὕτως πολὺ διαφέρει ὁ θεὸς τῆς ἀνθρωπότητος· καὶ καθάπερ ὁ ἥλιος πλήρης πάντοτε διαμένει μὴ ἐλάσων γινόμενος, οὕτως πάντοτε ὁ θεὸς τέλειος διαμένει, πλήρης ὤν· πάσης δυνάμεως καὶ συνέσεως καὶ σοφίας καὶ ἀθανασίας καὶ πάντων τῶν ἀγαθῶν. Ἡ δὲ σελήνη κατὰ μῆνα φθίνει καὶ δυνάμει ἀποθνήσκει, ἐν τύπῳ οὖσα ἀνθρώπου, ἔπειτα ἀναγεννᾶται καὶ αὔξει εἰς δεῖγμα τῆς μελλούσης ἔσεσθαι ἀναστάσεως. Ὡσαύτως καὶ αἱ τρεῖς ἡμέραι πρὸ τῶν φωστήρων γεγονυῖαι τύποι εἰσὶν τῆς τριάδος, τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ λόγου αὐτοῦ καὶ τῆς σοφίας αὐτοῦ. Τετάρτῳ δὲ τύπῳ ἐστὶν ἄνθρωπος ὁ προσδεὴς τοῦ φωτός, ἵνα ᾖ θεός, λόγος, σοφία, ἄνθρωπος. Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ τετάρτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγενήθησαν φωστῆρες. Ἡ δὲ τῶν ἄστρων θέσις οἰκονομίαν καὶ τάξιν ἔχει τῶν δικαίων καί εὐσεβῶν καὶ τηρούντων τὸν νόμον καὶ τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ θεοῦ. Οἱ γὰρ ἐπιφανεῖς ἀστέρες καὶ λαμπροί εἰσιν εἰς μίμησιν τῶν προφητῶν· διὰ τοῦτο καὶ μένουσιν ἀκλινεῖς, μὴ μεταβαίνοντες εἰς τόπον ἐκ τόπου. Οἱ δὲ ἑτέραν ἔχοντες τάξιν τῆς λαμπρότητος τύποι εἰσὶν τοῦ λαοῦ τῶν δικαίων. Οἰ δ᾿ αὖ μεταβαίνοντες καὶ φεύγοντες τόπον ἐκ τόπου, οἱ καὶ πλάνητες καλούμενοι, καὶ αὐτοὶ τύπος τυγχάνουσιν τῶν ἀφισταμένων ἀνθρώπων ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, καταλιπόντων τὸν νόμον καὶ τὰ προστάγματα αὐτοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: On the fourth day the luminaries came into being. Since God, being foreknowing, knew the foolish talk of the vain philosophers, that they were going to say that the things growing on the earth are from the elements, for the purpose of rejecting God; so that the truth might be shown, the plants and the seeds came into being before the elements; for the later things are not able to do the same things as the earlier things. These things, however, are a specimen and a type of a great mystery. For the sun is a type of God, and the moon is a type of a human being. And just as the sun differs much from the moon in power and glory, so God differs much from humanity; and just as the sun always remains full, not becoming less, so God always remains perfect, being full of all power and understanding and wisdom and immortality and all good things. The moon, however, wanes each month and dies in terms of power, being a type of a human being, then is reborn and grows as a specimen of the resurrection that is going to be. Similarly, the three days that came into being before the luminaries are types of the triad, of God and His Word and His Wisdom. On the fourth day, however, there is a type of humanity, who needs light, so that there might be God, Word, Wisdom, humanity. For this reason the luminaries also came into being on the fourth day. The position of the stars, however, has an economy and order of the righteous and pious and those keeping the law and the commandments of God. For the conspicuous and shining stars are an imitation of the prophets; for this reason they also remain unchanging, not moving from place to place. Those having a different order of brightness are types of the people of the righteous. But those moving and fleeing from place to place, who are also called wanderers, themselves become a type of humans who revolt from God, abandoning His law and commandments.

choices.why: translation that conveys the negative connotation

pass_b_english: On the fourth day God brought the luminaries into existence. Because God is foreknowing, He knew that vain philosophers would claim earthly growth originates from the elements in order to deny Him. To demonstrate the truth, He caused plants and seeds to appear before the elements, since what comes later cannot produce what came before.

These events serve as a specimen and type of a great mystery. The sun typifies God; the moon typifies humanity. Just as the sun far surpasses the moon in power and glory, so God far surpasses humanity. Just as the sun always remains full, never diminishing, so God always remains perfect, being full of all power, understanding, wisdom, immortality, and every good thing. The moon, by contrast, wanes each month and dies in power, typifying humanity; then it is reborn and waxes as a specimen of the coming resurrection.

Likewise, the three days that existed before the luminaries are types of the triad: God, His Word, and His Wisdom. On the fourth day there is a type of humanity, who needs light so that there may be God, Word, Wisdom, and humanity. For this reason the luminaries were also created on the fourth day.

The arrangement of the stars embodies an economy and order of the righteous, the pious, and those who keep God's law and commandments. The conspicuous, shining stars imitate the prophets; therefore they remain fixed, not moving from place to place. Stars of a different order of brightness typify the people of the righteous. But those that move and flee from place to place — the ones called wanderers — themselves become a type of humans who revolt from God, abandoning His law and commandments.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the complex theological arguments regarding the order of creation (plants/seeds before elements) and the typological relationships (sun/God, moon/man, stars/prophets/righteous/wanderers). Pass B's slight stylistic variations (e.g., 'God brought the luminaries into existence' for 'ἐγένοντο') do not alter the meaning or agency established in the Greek.
